title: Shift compatibility of normalized scalar limit constraints
statement: Fix a prime l, finite extensions E⊆F of Q_l with embedding i, a compactification c of X→Y, an E whole-system reduction calculus S on X, and e∈N. In the setup of [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-maps] with the shifts of [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-structures], each specified natural transformation commutes with every integer shift: scalarCompletion(l,E,F,i,Y).hom (ordinary/complete scalar balancing), scalarLimitTensor(l,E,F,i,Y).hom (the tensor/total-limit constraint), scalarLimitRestriction(l,E,Y,e) (forward arithmetic restriction, with no e≥1 hypothesis), and scalarSupportLimit(l,E,c,S).hom (completed support restricted to constants compared to the actual strict total limit). Composite shifts are the indicated canonical composite structures, in particular the target of scalarCompletion uses normalized completed scalar extension followed by exact constant restriction. Underlying definitions are those of [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-maps], [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-structures]. For positive e and ramification data, the actual scalarLimitArrow component commutes with integer shifts, after composing the tensor/limit constraint with the strict arrow and inverse cofinal restriction.

proof.text: Total derived inverse limit is an exact functor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its unit-normalized composition constraints commute with shifts on K-injective representatives; [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] then gives compatibility of their whiskered composites. Its canonical comparison can be computed by shifting a K-injective tower resolution: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift] ensures that this is again such a resolution, and termwise inverse limit commutes with $[r]$. For the explicit Roos realization, countable products are exact on the pro-etale module site by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. The zigzag of [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] has arrows applying the resolution map to both cone coordinates and the augmentation from the termwise limit with zero extra coordinate. The former commutes with the signed cone shift because it is diagonal; the latter does because its signed coordinate is zero, by [lem-weil-roos-comm-shift]. Thus the explicit Roos shift and the canonical total-derived-limit shift coincide under this zigzag. No uniqueness of a cone in a triangulated category is used.

proof.text: Consider the specified cofinal map and tensor/product map in [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality]. The former has product-arrow components $a_e(x)_n=x_{en}$ and $b_e(y)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}t_{en}\cdots t_{i-1}y_i$. Both are degree-zero maps commuting with the termwise shift: each summand has the same coefficient and transition before and after shifting. The product comparison is characterized by its projections as in [lem-weil-product-comm-shift]. On the unshifted-product coordinate $x$ the Roos shift is this product comparison, and on the extra shifted-product coordinate $y$ it is $(-1)^r$ times this comparison, by [lem-weil-roos-comm-shift]. Consequently the square for $r_e$ is diagonal with identical signs on its two routes. The finite-free tensor/product comparison has projections $\mathrm{pr}_n\otimes1_B$; tensoring by degree-zero $B$ and these projections commute with $[r]$. On its two cone summands the same diagonal sign calculation gives its shift square. Since $r_e$ is invertible in the derived category, compose its square with $r_e^{-1}$ on both appropriate sides to obtain the square for the specified inverse.

proof.text: For the remaining ordinary/completed scalar comparison, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies the actual $\chi_{F/E,N}$ on a K-flat representative $P$ with its compatible quotient product map and zero extra Roos coordinate. Apply [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift] to this very quotient map. Its product coordinate commutes with shift by the degree-zero tensor formula, and its other coordinate remains zero after multiplication by $(-1)^r$. It follows that $\chi$ commutes with the prescribed shifts, including the cone sign. The shift on its strict-tower target is the one in [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]; the scalar comparison on its source is the one of Step 1, since its K-flat computation has exactly that counit square. Thus this calculation compares the chosen morphisms, with the normalized source and target structures, on all resolving representatives and hence in the derived category.

proof.text: The actual scalarSupportLimit is the composite of scalarCompletedLimitRestriction and scalarSystemRestrictionComp whiskered by the native support functor. The first is constructed from the normalized derived-composite maps and the ordinary exact restriction/limit map; the second is the exact derived composition iso. On shifted resolutions every constituent has the same degreewise restriction and composition square, and the unique normalized descents give these squares for the specified maps. Compose and whisker them to obtain the support/limit square.

Apply [lem-pur-strict-scalar-mate-shift] to the actual strict arrow. Whisker by total limit and compose with the tensor/limit square and inverse arithmetic restriction. The associators have identity components; hence the composed transformation has exactly scalarLimitArrow as its component. Cancel intermediate shift comparisons to obtain the displayed total-limit square.
